passage: Monday's team meeting in the Osaka office had nine people around the table. Yuki-san was going through the client figures when the slide stopped on Aiko's chart. "This total is wrong. Aiko, you've counted March twice." A few heads turned. Aiko felt heat climb from her neck to her ears. She'd checked it. Hadn't she? She opened her mouth, then pressed her lips together and bowed slightly. "I'm sorry. I'll fix it." The meeting moved on. That evening on the crowded train home, and later in the shower, she kept replaying it. I could have said, 'Thank you, I'll send a corrected version by noon.' Or, 'Could we go over it after the meeting?' Anything but that small bow.

qa.q: What error did Yuki-san point out in Aiko's chart?
qa.a: Aiko had counted March twice.

qa.q: What was Aiko feeling as heat climbed from her neck to her ears?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and exposed in front of nine people, with a flash of doubt about whether she really had checked it.

qa.q: What could Aiko do next to move on from this moment?
qa.a: Rather than only replaying it, she could fix the figure and ask Yuki-san for a short private word about checking totals, turning the sting into learning.

qa.q: What might the correction have been like from Yuki-san's side?
qa.a: Yuki-san may simply have wanted the figures right for the client and not noticed how a public correction felt to a new intern.

grounding: A young woman is corrected in front of her team, feels her face burn, swallows her reply and spends the evening rehearsing better ones.

passage: The Friday staff meeting at the Indore school was running late. Vaibhav sir, the senior maths teacher, held up the Class 7 test paper Yamini had set. "Question five has two correct answers. The trainee should have had it checked." Twelve teachers looked at her. Yamini's face burned. She'd given it to him on Tuesday to check, and he hadn't said anything. The words were right there, but she swallowed them and nodded. That night, grading copies at her kitchen table, she said the sentence out loud to the empty room: "I did give it to you on Tuesday, sir." Then a calmer version. Then a sharper one. By midnight she'd rehearsed six replies and used none of them.

qa.q: Which question on the test paper had two correct answers?
qa.a: Question five had two correct answers.

qa.q: Why did Yamini say the sentence out loud to the empty room that night?
qa.a: She felt humiliated and unfairly blamed, and rehearsing replies was her way of handling the anger she had swallowed in the meeting.

qa.q: What might be a wise next step for Yamini after this public correction?
qa.a: She could ask Vaibhav sir for a short private talk, calmly mention she shared it on Tuesday, and ask how checking should work in future.

qa.q: What might the other teachers have thought when they saw Yamini nod silently?
qa.a: Some may have assumed she made a careless mistake, while others might have noticed her burning face and felt uneasy about the public correction.

grounding: A trainee teacher is corrected in front of the staff, swallows her reply and spends the night rehearsing what she could have said.

passage:
"Before we close, slide six," Rekha said to the room. "Lalremsiami, these totals are wrong. The client would have caught that. Please be more careful."
Five people looked at Lalremsiami. Her face went hot.
"I, yes. Sorry." She wanted to say the data came late. She didn't.
That night, in the hostel room, her roommate found her talking to the mirror.
"Siami? Who are you talking to?"
"Rekha. I'm saying what I should have said. 'The sheet came at 11 p.m. I asked for it on Monday.'"
"You've said that four times."
"I'll say it forty."

qa.q: Which slide did Rekha point out?
qa.a: Slide six.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling when five people looked at her?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and humiliated, her face hot, and swallowed the reply she wanted to give.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Lalremsiami after the meeting?
qa.a: Instead of rehearsing the reply alone, she could calmly ask Rekha for a short private talk about the late data and the error.

qa.q: What is it like for the roommate to find Lalremsiami at the mirror?
qa.a: The roommate is probably surprised and a little worried, seeing how much the meeting still stings.

grounding: Shows an intern corrected in front of the team, swallowing her reply, then rehearsing it all evening.

passage:
It was only a small mistake. I'd put last year's date on the brochure draft. But Bidisha ma'am noticed it on the big screen in the Monday meeting, with the whole team there.
"Madhuri, who checked this? The date's wrong. Basic stuff."
I felt the heat climb my neck to my ears. I had an answer ready, that I'd copied the template she had sent me. But the words stuck. I just said, "I'll fix it."
That evening, walking to the bus stop, I said the whole speech to myself. Twice on the bus. Once in the shower. I made it better each time, sharper, braver. Looking back, that girl never said a single one of those speeches out loud.

qa.q: What mistake was on the brochure draft?
qa.a: Last year's date.

qa.q: What does the heat climbing Madhuri's neck suggest?
qa.a: Madhuri felt embarrassed and hurt at being corrected in front of the whole team.

qa.q: What went wrong after the meeting, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Madhuri rehearsed her speech alone again and again; a calm private word with Bidisha ma'am about the template would help more.

qa.q: What might Bidisha ma'am have been thinking in the meeting?
qa.a: She may have been stressed about quality and not noticed how public correction would sting a junior.

grounding: Shows an intern publicly corrected in a meeting, swallowing her reply and rehearsing it all evening.

passage:
Team lead's note, Wednesday
In this morning's review, Mr Kulkarni pointed out an error in Ayesha's supplier table in front of all eight of us: "This is wrong. Did you even check?" Ayesha went very red, opened her mouth, then closed it. She stared at her laptop for the rest of the meeting and did not speak again. At lunch she ate alone at her desk, typing and deleting something on her phone.
The error was real. The public tone was hard. I am noting this because she is new and may not know that it's okay to raise it. I will check in with her tomorrow and suggest she ask him for a private conversation.
Rajni

qa.q: How many people were in the review?
qa.a: Eight.

qa.q: What does Ayesha opening and closing her mouth suggest?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and hurt, and swallowed a reply she wanted to make.

qa.q: What does Rajni plan to do next, and why could it help?
qa.a: Check in with Ayesha tomorrow and suggest a private talk with Mr Kulkarni, so she doesn't carry it alone.

qa.q: What might Mr Kulkarni have been focused on when he pointed out the error?
qa.a: He was probably focused on the real error and the supplier deadline, not noticing how public criticism lands on a new intern.

grounding: Shows a team lead's note on an intern corrected publicly, who swallows her reply and stays upset through the day.

passage:
Tuesday night.
At the ten o'clock team meeting, Rehana ma'am put my slide on the big screen and said, "Manjula, this total is off by a whole column. Everyone, please double-check the interns' sheets." Eight people turned to look at me. My face went hot, right up to my ears. I had an answer ready, that I used the old template she sent last month, but it stuck in my throat and all I said was "okay".
Now it's nearly midnight and I've said it properly about twenty times: on the bus, in the shower, while Amma was asking me about dinner. In my head I am calm and clever. In that room I was a statue.
Tomorrow I sit at the same table again. I don't know how to look at her.

qa.q: What did Rehana ask everyone to do in the meeting?
qa.a: She asked everyone to double-check the interns' sheets.

qa.q: What does Manjula's rehearsing late into the night suggest about how Manjula feels?
qa.a: Manjula feels humiliated and frustrated for freezing, so the calm, clever reply keeps replaying long after the meeting.

qa.q: What could Manjula try before tomorrow's meeting?
qa.a: Manjula could ask Rehana for a few minutes alone to explain the old template calmly, instead of only rehearsing it at night.

qa.q: What might the correction have looked like from Rehana's side?
qa.a: Rehana may have seen it as a quick quality check for the whole team, without noticing how exposed it left Manjula.

grounding: Shows an error pointed out in front of the team, a hot face and a swallowed reply, then an evening spent rehearsing the answer.
